variants.text:
Talk about making love before you do it

From here on, when I say making love, I'm talking about two people who care about each other deeply and feel super connected, using their bodies as part of that connection. If you’ve never experienced this, it may be like trying to explain the taste of an orange. If you don’t know what love is, you don’t know. That’s another conversation, and I'd suggest reading my inner child reparenting guide. Having sex is just the physical act, whether that connection is there or not, although sometimes sex can create the connection too.

Most couples don’t talk honestly about sex until they’re already having it. Bad timing. Now saying what you actually want might interrupt the whole thing, disappoint somebody, or turn a moment of passion into a negotiation.

The biggest question, to me, is basically the one my dad was trying to give me when I was five: Would we actually like to raise children together, and are we ready? I wish I'd taken that question more literally more often. If I can't even talk with a woman about it before we have sex, that's already useful information about how little we know about what we're doing.

Once we're really having that conversation, the other sex stuff has somewhere to go. What does sex mean to each of us? Is there anything important about what makes our bodies relax or shut down, our pasts, kinks, or something that just doesn't work? “I don’t know, but I’m willing to find out honestly with you” is a fine answer. Desire changes too. At some point one of us may want more, less, or something different, and I’d rather know we can talk about that than discover we can’t after resentment has been quietly growing for six months.

And can we still say the uncomfortable thing once we're naked and one of us is afraid of disappointing the other? That's the part I care about more than whether our bodies happen to fit perfectly.

All of this advice sounds a lot easier before the woman is actually in front of me. I pretty much always intend to wait long enough to figure out who I'm dealing with, and then the heat of the moment hits and I just want to please her. I'll get to that problem later.
